The ribbon along the top of the main window: tabs, each holding the
        application's commands for one area of work in labelled groups.

    shape: {RibbonShape}

shape RibbonShape:
    description:
        A ribbon runs along the top of the window, using gpui-kit's Tab
        component with its default styling. Its tabs are, in order: Project,
        collapsed ribbon.

    projectIndicator:
        To the left of the tabs, in the same bar, sits the @{ProjectIndicator},
        with a thin vertical divider between it and the first tab.

    groups:
        (Cmd+F1 on macOS). Whether it is collapsed is one of the
        @{UserPreferencesScope}.

        Collapsed, the tabs go away too. The ribbon becomes a single thin row
        led by the project indicator, as it is beside the tabs and with the same
        divider after it, and then holding every primary command, from all of
        the tabs, as small buttons: a small icon beside its label, and dark mode
        as a small switch. They keep the order of their tabs, with a thin
        vertical divider between the commands of one tab and the next, and keep
        their tooltips and disabled states. The chevron sits at the right end of
        the row. Every control in the row, the chevron and the dividers
        included, is vertically centred in it.

content.text:
The ribbon tabs are back to gpui-kit's default behaviour, with only the theme's colours. The project indicator now sits on a darker background with no right-side border. The tab code is identical to the last commit, before my border changes, so tab labels should no longer hop as tabs open and close.

**Project indicator** (`src/ribbon/mod.rs`)
- **Expanded ribbon:** the indicator and the activity spinner beside it sit on a darker strip the full height of the tab bar, with no divider before the first tab. The change of background marks the edge.
- **Darker colour:** I used the theme's "pressed" grey (#3c3c3c dark, #c6c6c6 light), a step darker than the tab bar in both modes. The other dark greys get lighter in light mode.
- **Collapsed ribbon:** the indicator has the same darker strip, and I removed the divider after it there too, to match. The dividers between each tab's commands stay.

**One side effect of default tabs:** when two open tabs sit next to each other (Project and Code, say), their borders show side by side, as gpui-kit draws them. I've written that exception into the Theme scope's "a line is never doubled" rule, and removed the double-border checks from the ribbon tests.

**Checked:**
- **Pictures:** I drew the ribbon expanded and collapsed, in dark and light mode, with Project and Code open. The darker strip, missing divider and default tabs all show as expected. The hop itself was about positions from frame to frame, so I haven't confirmed it's gone on screen.
- **Test:** `ribbon_tabs_are_drawn_beside_the_project_indicator` now checks, in both modes, that:
  - the indicator's area has the darker background and no border;
  - the selected Project tab is drawn straight after it.
- **Everything else:** all 190 tests pass (1 ignored), the release build has no warnings, and `piton check`, `piton build check` and `piton build` pass.

**Spec:** the Ribbon scope now says:
- tabs keep gpui-kit's own borders and spacing, and nothing adds or removes any;
- the indicator sits on a darker background with no divider, both beside the tabs and in the collapsed row.
